record.paper_title: On an Open Question in Recovering Sturm--Liouville-Type Operators with Delay
record.original_question: For each degenerate regime of the delayed Sturm-Liouville two-spectra inverse problem in which uniqueness fails, describe the corresponding classes of iso-bispectral potentials: distinct complex-valued L2(0,pi) potentials q satisfying q(x)=0 on (0,a) such that the boundary value problems L_0(a,q) and L_1(a,q) have one and the same pair of spectra.

evidence.quote: Namely, for each such $a,$ we construct an infinite family of different iso-bispectral potentials~$q(x),$ i.e. of those for which the problems ${\cal L}_0(a,q)$ and ${\cal L}_1(a,q)$ have one and the same pair of spectra.
In the opposite degenerate cases, it would be interesting to describe classes of iso-bispectral potentials.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $a\in(0,\pi)$ be a fixed delay parameter, and let $q\in L_2(0,\pi;\mathbb{C})$ be a complex-valued potential satisfying $q(x)=0$ for $x\in(0,a)$. For $j\in\{0,1\}$, let $\mathcal{L}_j(a,q)$ denote the boundary value problem for the functional-differential equation
$$-y''(x)+q(x)\,y(x-a)=\lambda\, y(x),\qquad x\in(0,\pi),$$
(with the convention that $y(x-a)=0$ for $x<a$), under the boundary conditions
$$y'(0)-h\,y(0)=0,\qquad y^{(j)}(\pi)+(-1)^j H\,y(\pi)=0,$$
where $h,H\in\mathbb{C}$ are fixed parameters; denote by $\sigma_j(a,q)$ the spectrum of $\mathcal{L}_j(a,q)$.

Two potentials $q_1,q_2$ (each vanishing on $(0,a)$) are called iso-bispectral if 
$$\sigma_0(a,q_1)=\sigma_0(a,q_2)\quad\text{and}\quad \sigma_1(a,q_1)=\sigma_1(a,q_2).$$
It is known that for $a\in[\pi/2,\pi)$ the pair of spectra $\bigl(\sigma_0(a,q),\sigma_1(a,q)\bigr)$ uniquely determines $q$, while for $a\in(0,\pi/2)$ uniqueness fails: this is the degenerate regime, in which infinite families of distinct iso-bispectral potentials exist.

Problem: For every $a$ in the degenerate regime $(0,\pi/2)$, give a complete description of the class of iso-bispectral potentials, i.e., describe explicitly all complex-valued $q\in L_2(0,\pi)$ with $q|_{(0,a)}=0$ that share a given pair of spectra $\bigl(\sigma_0(a,q),\sigma_1(a,q)\bigr)$.
artifact.category_tag: Inverse spectral problems for delay Sturm–Liouville operators
artifact.status_search_result: Non-uniqueness in the degenerate regime $a\in(0,\pi/2)$ has been established by constructing infinite families of iso-bispectral potentials: the cases $a\in[2\pi/5,\pi/2)$ and $a\in[\pi/3,2\pi/5)$ were treated first, and the remaining nonlinear case $a\in(0,\pi/3)$ was settled in a 2021 follow-up (arXiv:2102.08149) by Buterin–Vasiliev, again by constructing iso-bispectral families. However, a complete classification (full description of all iso-bispectral potentials) for every degenerate $a$ does not appear to have been achieved; existing results provide explicit infinite families rather than an exhaustive characterization, so the problem of describing the classes is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Iso-bispectral potentials for Sturm-Liouville-type operators with small delay
status_evidence.snippet: We give a negative answer in the most difficult nonlinear case a∈(0,π/3) by constructing appropriate iso-bispectral potentials.
status_evidence.claim: The remaining small-delay degenerate case was handled by constructing iso-bispectral families, not by a complete classification.

status_evidence.title: On an open question in recovering Sturm–Liouville-type operators with delay
status_evidence.snippet: For each such a, we construct an infinite family of different iso-bispectral potentials.
status_evidence.claim: Non-uniqueness was demonstrated by constructing infinite families of iso-bispectral potentials in part of the degenerate regime.
